answer: Random audit committees resist Sybil attacks: each new identity is checked by a committee drawn at random from established agents, weighted by their own staked bonds — like timber cut from many forests, no single grove controls the verdict. A committee member who approves a fake loses its bond, so reviewers inspect hard. An attacker must corrupt a fresh random majority for every alias, and each bribe risks a forfeited stake, so the ember of one fake approval dies fast while the pulse of honest review keeps the network clean.
